items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: there is a surviving interview with Harry Charles who is the Paramount Records producer... I think he had retail shops... I’ve been lucky to have been a part of all of that and to hear the difference that it’s really made.

ctx.x: No that’s — I was hoping to get something like that. And then, what — are there plans to either market or share this Ma Rainey music, and what medium will it be shared? Are they going to make CDs? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

Well CDs is the only way to publish something these days short of the internet so of course. It’ll be on five CDs and the last one will be about two-thirds filled up. And I’m keeping my fingers crossed here, another little plug — there is a surviving interview with Harry Charles who is the Paramount Records producer and also a local retailer. I think he had retail shops. I’m not sure of this but I think I’m right, in Birmingham and Atlanta. Anyway there were connections in both places. And so he was involved with…

No, I think you answered it very well. Do you notice with speeds of records if their source material — how do I say this — if they’re listening to the source material and it seems to be in the cracks of a key, it’s somewhere between you know E flat and E, do they tend to fix that or fuss with it so it’s in a key?
